The midpoint of $A(2,-3)$ and $B(x,y)$ is $(5,1)$. Find the coordinates of $B$.
Find the gradient of the line through $(2,-1)$ and $(6,7)$.
Find the equation of the line through $(4,3)$ with gradient $-2$, in the form $y=mx+c$.
Find the equation of the line through $(-1,4)$ and $(3,-4)$, in the form $y=mx+c$.
Find the equation of the line parallel to $y=3x-1$ passing through $(5,0)$.
questions.answer: Parallel lines share the same gradient, $m=3$: $y-0=3(x-5)$, so $y=3x-15$.

questions.q: Find the equation of the line perpendicular to $y=\dfrac{1}{3}x+2$ passing through $(6,-1)$.
questions.answer: The perpendicular gradient is the negative reciprocal: $m=-3$. $y-(-1)=-3(x-6)$, so $y=-3x+18-1=-3x+17$.

questions.q: Determine whether the lines $y=4x-3$ and $4y+x=8$ are parallel, perpendicular, or neither.
questions.answer: Rewrite the second line as $y=-\dfrac{1}{4}x+2$, gradient $-\dfrac{1}{4}$. The product of the gradients is $4\times\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right)=-1$, so the lines are perpendicular.

A circle has equation $(x+1)^2+(y-4)^2=49$. State its center and radius.

A circle has center $(0,0)$ and radius 5. Determine whether the line $y=x+8$ intersects the circle, is tangent to it, or misses it entirely, by comparing the distance from the center to the line against the radius.
questions.answer: Rewrite the line as $x-y+8=0$. Distance from $(0,0)$: $d=\dfrac{|0-0+8|}{\sqrt{1^2+(-1)^2}}=\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{2}}=4\sqrt{2}\approx5.66$. Since $5.66>5$ (the distance exceeds the radius), the line misses the circle entirely.

questions.q: A circle has center $(2,1)$ and radius 3. Determine whether the line $x+y=10$ intersects the circle, is tangent to it, or misses it entirely.
questions.answer: Rewrite the line as $x+y-10=0$. Distance from $(2,1)$: $d=\dfrac{|2+1-10|}{\sqrt{1^2+1^2}}=\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{7\sqrt{2}}{2}\approx4.95$. Since $4.95>3$, the line misses the circle entirely.

questions.q: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $A(1,2)$ and $B(7,8)$.
questions.answer: Midpoint: $(4,5)$. Gradient of $AB$: $\dfrac{8-2}{7-1}=1$. Perpendicular gradient: $-1$. Equation: $y-5=-1(x-4)$, so $y=-x+9$.

questions.q: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $A(-2,3)$ and $B(4,-5)$.
questions.answer: Midpoint: $(1,-1)$. Gradient of $AB$: $\dfrac{-5-3}{4-(-2)}=\dfrac{-8}{6}=-\dfrac{4}{3}$. Perpendicular gradient: $\dfrac{3}{4}$. Equation: $y+1=\dfrac{3}{4}(x-1)$, so $y=\dfrac{3}{4}x-\dfrac{7}{4}$.

sections.heading: Area of a triangle from coordinates

questions.q: Find the area of the triangle with vertices $P(0,0)$, $Q(8,0)$, $R(3,6)$.
questions.answer: Using the coordinate area formula: Area $=\dfrac{1}{2}|x_P(y_Q-y_R)+x_Q(y_R-y_P)+x_R(y_P-y_Q)|=\dfrac{1}{2}|0(0-6)+8(6-0)+3(0-0)|=\dfrac{1}{2}(48)=24$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: locating a cell tower

questions.q: This question has two parts. Two houses are located at $A(0,0)$ and $B(12,0)$ (positions in kilometers). A cell tower must be built equidistant from both houses, and it must also lie on the line $y=x+2$. (a) Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, and use it together with $y=x+2$ to find the tower's coordinates. (b) Find the distance from the tower to each house, and confirm they are equal.
questions.answer: (a) Midpoint of $AB$: $(6,0)$. Since $AB$ is horizontal, its perpendicular bisector is the vertical line $x=6$. Substituting into $y=x+2$: $y=8$. Tower location: $(6,8)$. (b) Distance to $A$: $\sqrt{(6-0)^2+(8-0)^2}=\sqrt{36+64}=\sqrt{100}=10$ km. Distance to $B$: $\sqrt{(6-12)^2+(8-0)^2}=\sqrt{36+64}=\sqrt{100}=10$ km. Both distances equal 10 km, confirming the tower is equidistant from both houses.
